title: Non-Invasive Hemodynamic Assessment in Cardiogenic Shock
official: Non-Invasive Hemodynamic Assessment in Cardiogenic Shock: Validation and Artificial Intelligence-Driven Innovations (HD-ASSESS-CS)
summary: Pulmonary artery catheter (PAC) monitoring is the reference standard for hemodynamic assessment in cardiogenic shock (CS), but it is invasive, resource-demanding and not universally available. HD-ASSESS-CS is a prospective, observational, multicenter study that will enroll consecutive adult patients with CS or pre-shock in whom PAC monitoring is clinically indicated. In each patient, a standardized comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography will be performed in close temporal proximity to invasive measurements, at baseline and at repeated time points during hospitalization. The study will assess the agreement between echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic parameters, develop novel multiparametric echocardiographic indices (strain, Doppler and cardiac time intervals), and explore artificial intelligence models for automated estimation of hemodynamics from echocardiographic images. PAC placement is not performed for research purposes and AI outputs are not used for patient care.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Clinical diagnosis of cardiogenic shock or pre-shock
* Clinical indication for invasive hemodynamic monitoring with a pulmonary artery catheter according to standard of care
* Written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Refusal or inability to provide informed consent
* No clinical indication for pulmonary artery catheter monitoring
